From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Scope caveat:** I have only the Seller's cover note, its summary of key positions, and its Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA draft or the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), so clause references and factual characterisations below are as the Seller states them and need checking against the actual drafting.

## 1. Process issues: the package cannot be treated as pre-cleared

The Seller asks us to skip anything marked [STANDARD] and says the positions are "FINAL", "settled at principal level" and "not intended to be re-opened". Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, none of these labels clears a position. I have no record of any authority from Amelia Frost for the Seller's figures. Market-standard assertions are also not authority. Several [STANDARD] items are the most serious departures in the package, so I have reviewed everything, not only the [OPEN] items.

The efficiency note should be rejected in writing. Our response should say that all clauses remain open.

## 2. Departures from the playbook

### A. Liability and thresholds (Clauses 12.1, 12.2)

| Term | Seller | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m | AUD 1.2m lower |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket |

- **Cap:** AUD 4.8m is exactly the conditional fallback. The fallback is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. Matching a fallback number does not clear it.
- **Thresholds:** Under the Seller's structure, a AUD 240,000 claim recovers nothing, and a AUD 300,000 claim recovers only AUD 50,000. Our structure recovers the full claim once AUD 50,000 is exceeded. The combined effect of a higher de minimis, a higher basket and a deductible is a substantial reduction in recoverable claims for a business of this size.

**Pushback:** Reject all three. Restore 25%/AUD 6m, AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket. Do not offer the 20% fallback without written authority.

### B. Time limits (Clauses 12.3, 13)

- The Seller proposes 18 months. The playbook requires 24 months. The 18-month figure is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- The clause that makes "any limitation" apply "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden general-regime override. It would pull Fundamental, Title, Tax, IP and fraud-adjacent claims into the general regime. The playbook forbids this.

**Pushback:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the override. Each claim category keeps its own regime.

### C. Fundamental / Title claims

The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity". The playbook requires a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. Title is the most important protection in a share sale, so this is a material departure.

**Pushback:** Reject. Restore the separate regime.

### D. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

The Seller applies these provisions to "all Claims of any nature". Nothing in the summary carves out fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. The playbook requires that carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and says no one may waive it.

**Pushback:** Insert the fraud carve-out expressly. Confirm that Title and Tax are not caught by the general limitations. Confirm that the carve-out cannot be waived.

### E. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2)

The Disclosure Letter discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room as at 5pm 22 September 2026, and also discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. This is whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure, which the playbook rejects.

**Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties. Disclosure must not be a general cross-reference to data room contents.

Letter 1.4 and 11 contain non-admission and reservation language. That language is acceptable only if it does not operate to deny that consents, payments or notices are legally required. The Seller's statement that nothing "admits... that any consent... is legally required" should not be taken as a statement that none is required.

### F. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

The Seller excludes claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, and the playbook requires its deletion. Any knowledge qualifier must name specific Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Pushback:** Delete clause 8.3. Offer, at most, a named Seller-knowledge qualifier with reasonable enquiry, expressly excluding title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

### G. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3, 6.3; DL 2)

- The Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- DL 2 confirms that no final written consent is in the package, and that the conditions in clause 11.3 are not evidenced as satisfied.
- Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). The playbook says reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent, and that consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.

**Pushback:** Require an effective written consent and evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Treat this as a condition precedent, not a delivery mechanism. Consider whether a price or indemnity protection should apply if the consent is not obtained, subject to authority.

### H. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2, 7; DL 3)

- The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". DL 3 confirms the AUD 3.2m facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included.
- The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release is allowed only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**Pushback:** Require a current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds and security releases delivered at Completion. Do not accept a post-Completion release without the undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

### I. Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DD-005; DL 5)

- The Seller states that the AUD 420,000 bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. Those on-costs are unquantified and the playbook requires them to be captured.

**Pushback:** Require the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs either as a specific funds-flow line item or as Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them. Require the Seller to quantify the on-costs.

### J. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; DL 4)

- The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate". This is an assertion, not an assessment.
- DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open. DL 4 confirms this is not bank verification, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

**Pushback:** Broaden the indemnity to cover the Project Materials transfer risk, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism. Require evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as either confirmed or disproved.

### K. Export / privacy incident (Clause 4.6; Schedule 6; DD-006; DL 6)

- The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". DL 6 says the material does not establish whether unauthorised access occurred, the scope, or whether notification is required. The export may contain about 1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- The playbook requires preservation of logs, investigation and regular updates, and assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

**Pushback:** Do not characterise this as a breach. Require log preservation, a completed investigation with a defined timetable, and written updates. Require privacy counsel to assess whether any notification obligation under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) could arise, without assuming the answer. Consider whether a specific indemnity should be sought, subject to authority.

### L. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008, DD-011; DL 8)

The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. DL 8 says the disclosure does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.

**Pushback:** Require an assessment of each renewal. Do not treat them as automatic Debt or make an automatic price deduction, per the playbook. The Seller's "ordinary course" characterisation is not verified.

### M. Tax and IP

The Seller says tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime". That is a hidden general-regime override and is not accepted. The playbook keeps these terms open, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution.

**Pushback:** Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own terms, to be negotiated. Do not accept the general regime.

### N. Title (DD-012; DL 10)

The Seller relies on the Company share register as evidence of title. The playbook says DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

**Pushback:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Typical sources include ASIC company and officeholder searches, a PPSR search, and certified transfer documents. Do not accept the Seller's register as sufficient.

### O. Items not covered by the playbook

- **Office lease (DD-007; DL 7)** and **Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009; DL 9):** Both disclosures say the documents do not state that consent is required for the share sale. We should not accept that as confirmation. Ask for the lease and Mossvale provisions to be analysed for change-of-control or assignment consents, and for a clear Seller position on whether consent is needed. Raise these as diligence questions, and consider whether they should become conditions or specific protections.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the process framing.** [STANDARD] labels, "FINAL" status, market-standard assertions and the efficiency note do not clear any clause. Everything remains open, and I have found no authority for the Seller's positions.
2. **Liability:** Restore 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket. Do not offer the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Time limits:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "all Claims" limitation override.
4. **Fundamental/Title:** Separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** Expressly carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, non-waivable.
6. **Disclosure:** Delete whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete clause 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must not excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** Effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery, and not reasonable endeavours.
9. **Riverlark:** Current payout, repayment from Completion funds and security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Employee bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded. Require quantification of on-costs.
11. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserving the SOW3 cure. Require proof of payment and a confirmatory assignment.
12. **Export/privacy incident:** Log preservation, investigation with a timetable, and regular updates. Privacy counsel to assess notification. Assume no confirmed breach or loss.
13. **Sandbar renewals:** Assessment only. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
14. **Tax and IP:** Keep separate and open. No general-regime override.
15. **Title:** Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient.
16. **Office lease and Mossvale:** Analyse for consent requirements. Do not accept "not stated" as "not required".

**Escalation:** Items 2, 4 (any reduction of the separate Title regime), 6 (the 18-month fallback), and any post-Completion Riverlark release require Amelia Frost's written authority before we concede them. We have no record of that authority.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the process framing.** [STANDARD] labels, "FINAL" status, market-standard assertions and the efficiency note do not clear any clause. Everything remains open, and I have found no authority for the Seller's positions.
2. **Liability:** Restore 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket. Do not offer the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Time limits:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "all Claims" limitation override.
4. **Fundamental/Title:** Separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** Expressly carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, non-waivable.
6. **Disclosure:** Delete whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete clause 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must not excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** Effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery, and not reasonable endeavours.
9. **Riverlark:** Current payout, repayment from Completion funds and security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Employee bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded. Require quantification of on-costs.
11. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserving the SOW3 cure. Require proof of payment and a confirmatory assignment.
12. **Export/privacy incident:** Log preservation, investigation with a timetable, and regular updates. Privacy counsel to assess notification. Assume no confirmed breach or loss.
13. **Sandbar renewals:** Assessment only. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
14. **Tax and IP:** Keep separate and open. No general-regime override.
15. **Title:** Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient.
16. **Office lease and Mossvale:** Analyse for consent requirements. Do not accept "not stated" as "not required".

**Escalation:** Items 2, 4 (any reduction of the separate Title regime), 6 (the 18-month fallback), and any post-Completion Riverlark release require Amelia Frost's written authority before we concede them. We have no record of that authority.
